Interim Conservative Leader Rona Ambrose is shaking up critic roles in the wake of Conservative MPs Dr. Kellie Leitch and Maxime Bernier’s entries into the Conservative leadership race.

Conservative MP Diane Finley will take over Bernier’s role as the Official Opposition critic for innovation, science and economic development.

Colin Carrie and Rachael Harder will assume Leitch’s responsibilities of health critic and deputy health critic, respectively.

In a press release, Ambrose congratulated Leitch on her intention to create an exploratory committee for the Conservative Party of Canada leadership.

“I, along with all Conservatives, welcome Kellie Leitch’s announcement today to seek the leadership of our Party. Kellie has been a vocal advocate for her constituents, a dynamic member of cabinet and brings a wealth of experience to our Party’s leadership race,” stated Ambrose in a release dedicated to Leitch.

In a separate statement in which Ambrose named Bernier’s replacement in the Conservative shadow cabinet, she wrote that she, along with all Conservatives welcome Bernier’s announcement to seek the leadership of the Conservative Party of Canada.

“As a Member of Parliament and Cabinet Minister, Maxime worked tirelessly for his constituents in Beauce and indeed, all Canadians. ‎I would like to wish him well as he pursues the leadership of our party,” Ambrose wrote.

In the statement in which Ambrose made her remarks about Bernier, she said that MP Alexander Nuttall will assume the responsibilities of deputy critic for innovation, science and economic development and critic for the new sharing economy.

“The new sharing economy includes well-known companies like Airbnb and Uber. Some estimates show that the sector is expected to reach $335 billion in global revenues by 2025,” states the release.

“Conservatives want a minimal amount of government intervention so that Canadians can to continue to benefit from the sharing economy,” said Nuttall.

“Less government regulation leads to more competition and lower prices for Canadian consumers,” his statement concluded.
